root_idea.summary: The root centers on making something absorb water or a comparable liquid, especially giving drink or supplying water.
root_idea.development: From the basic act of giving water, the lexicon develops distinctions between directly giving drink, making drink or a water source available, irrigating land, requesting water, and the vessels, places, shares, and agents associated with watering.

senses.definition: To give a person or animal drink; to cause someone to drink or be given drink.
senses.usage_conditions: The object may be water, milk, or another drink. The passive forms express being given drink. The expression may specify drink from what is in the bellies of animals.

senses.definition: To water or irrigate land, plants, or cultivated produce.
senses.usage_conditions: Used for supplying water to growing things, including irrigation by water running over or into the land.

senses.definition: To provide or make available drink or water, so that someone may take and use it as desired; to give someone access to a source of drink.
senses.usage_conditions: Form IV is presented as broader than directly putting drink to someone's mouth: it can make a river, water, or other drink available to the recipient. Passive forms express being supplied with drink.

senses.definition: To seek or request water or drink.
senses.usage_conditions: The request may be directed to a person who is asked to provide water.

senses.definition: The provision or service of giving drink, especially the provision of drink to pilgrims.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic pilgrimage context, the term can denote the service, office, or provision associated with giving drink rather than merely the liquid itself.

senses.definition: A vessel used for drinking, especially a drinking cup.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Joseph narrative it denotes the king's drinking-cup, also used as a measure.

senses.definition: A drink or an allotted share of water; a giving of drink.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrence, the term denotes the she-camel's allotted drink or water share.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become vehemently affected by sexual appetite.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tropical use of the Form I verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To send rain to someone, a land, or a people; to pray that rain be sent down.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in invocations and wishes for beneficial rain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pour water into a water-skin or other water container.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A construction describing filling a vessel with water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of sweat, to flow continuously without stopping.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive lexical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For the belly to become swollen with dropsy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The condition is described as yellow serum collecting in the belly; the related adjective can describe the swollen belly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a garment or piece of cloth absorb dye.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized use concerning the imbibing of coloring matter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To temper steel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical or later use recorded for the verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a person's heart imbibe enmity through repeated hostile treatment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tropical Form II construction, used when an objectionable action is repeatedly inflicted on someone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The giving of drink by one person to another, mutually.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal Form III verbal noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The joint drawing of water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional Form III noun for drawing water together.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cultivation arrangement in which one person manages the cultivation and watering of palms, vines, or similar plants for a specified share of the produce.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical agricultural contract.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To assign a well, stream, or other source of irrigation to someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction gives the person access to the source for drawing or using its water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause dropsy or yellow serum to develop in someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A medical use of the Form IV verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To give someone a hide or skin to make into a water-skin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object given is the material from which a سِقَاء is made.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To backbite or traduce someone, and impute a fault or vice to him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tropical and disapproved use of the Form IV verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To receive or absorb moisture or irrigation, becoming succulent or sappy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a thing that becomes thoroughly supplied with moisture; it may also describe skin drenched with blood.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of camels, to eat a fresh, moist plant and become fat from it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An assumed tropical application to animals feeding on moist vegetation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: They gave drink to one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal Form VI construction, with the drink distributed in full measure from the vessel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To draw water from a well or river.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This Form VIII use is distinct from Form X requesting water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become fat and satisfied through drinking water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tropical Form VIII use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ask, beg, or pray for rain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The conventional source of the expression for the prayer seeking rain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To force oneself to vomit or to vomit intentionally.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate Form X medical use, synonymous with deliberate emesis.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The towns, villages, or lands watered by the Euphrates.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized substantive use in the expression سَقْيُ الفُرَاتِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Drink, what is drunk, or what is given to drink; also a share or portion of water, especially an irrigation allotment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The irrigation sense may refer to the amount assigned to a tract of land or to animals.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Yellow serum or watery fluid occurring in the belly in dropsy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A medical noun for the fluid associated with the dropsical condition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The fluid contained in the birth membrane surrounding a young animal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized obstetrical use referring to the fluid that emerges with the membrane at birth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Land or produce irrigated by water running over the surface of the earth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Contrasted with land watered only by rainfall.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The sending down of rain upon people or land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in prayers for rain, including a rain of mercy rather than punishment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A skin or leather water-skin used for water or milk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can distinguish vessels made from one or more hides and has plural forms for such containers.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The stomach of a camel in which water is stored.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tropical application of the container sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cloud with large, forceful raindrops.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A descriptive adjective or noun for a rain-bearing cloud.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Papyrus, especially tender papyrus growing in or near water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plant name is linked lexically to its growth in water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Palm trees, especially palms irrigated by water-wheels.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plant noun or adjective derived from association with irrigation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bird said to draw water for itself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized bird name; later applications to particular large birds are reported in the lexicon.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who gives drink, a cup-bearer, water-carrier, or person who waters crops.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may denote the agent of supplying drink or irrigation; a proverb extends it to a person who does good.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A vein running from the interior of the head to the eye, whose severing causes loss of sight.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small channel, streamlet, or watercourse used to irrigate land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The channel is described as larger than a small jadwal and a watercourse; the word is also used for an irrigation water-wheel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Certain veins that discharge into the two abhar veins.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical plural use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A time or place of giving drink.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The related place noun may also occur in figurative expressions involving a drinking place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A stand or support made for water-jars, on which drinking mugs are hung.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A household or serving implement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Given drink, or watered or irrigated produce.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive participial adjective applied to recipients of drink and to plants or crops supplied with water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Tinged or suffused with redness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic expression describing a person marked with the redness of blood.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Basic giving, watering, and several explicitly stated tropical or constructional uses are represented.
Assigning a well or stream as a water source.
Giving a hide to make a water-skin.
Camels becoming fat from moist fodder.
Drawing water from a well or river.
Tropical fatness and satisfaction from water.
Adjectival description of a dropsical belly is covered by the dropsy meaning.
Giving of drink or drink allotment.
Place or service for giving drink.
Agent who gives drink or waters.
Time or place of giving drink.
Pointer plus an idiomatic drinking-place application.

cautions: Form I directly giving drink and Form IV making drink or a water source available are distinct constructions in the supplied Quran-focused evidence.
سِقَايَة has two Quranic uses here: the provision or service of giving drink and a drinking cup.
The Quranic Form X occurrences attest requesting water or drink; the separate classical rain-request use is listed outside the Quranic sense.
The Quranic سُقْيَا occurrence is represented as a drink or allotted water share; the separate classical rain-prayer use is kept distinct.
